# Joshua 18: verse-by-verse research notes

**Gaps to know about first:**
- **Missing sources:** I couldn't open the Enduring Word page for Joshua 18; only a short summary from its Joshua 18–19 page came up. I found nothing on this chapter from Catholic or Orthodox sites (newadvent, catholic.com, oca.org), bibleodyssey, the netbible notes, or any prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace teacher. Those sections are left out.
- **Where traditions differ:** I found no real disagreements between Protestant traditions on this chapter. Where a tradition's own teacher said something distinctive, I've marked it, for example "(Methodist)."
- **Thin coverage:** The pages I read say very little about vv. 12–15, 18 and 20–27, so most of those verses are missing below.

---

**v. 1: Shiloh and the Tent of Meeting**
- **Why Shiloh:** Barnes thinks Joshua chose it under God's direction (Deut 12:11), because Shiloh was unimportant enough to avoid jealousy between tribes, sat in the center of the land, and was secluded. He says its very name ("rest") was probably bestowed at this juncture when God had given the people rest from their enemies. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-1.htm)
- **God chose the place:** Benson says the move must have been by God's order, since God was to choose where the tabernacle stayed. He suggests God showed this through the Urim and Thummim. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-1.htm)
- **A center for the nation:** The Cambridge Bible sees the gathering as an act of homage and as setting up a center of national life. When loyalty to the tabernacle at Shiloh weakened, division and weakness followed. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-1.htm)
- **"Shiloh" and the Messiah (Methodist and Puritan):** Wesley links the name to the "Shiloh" of Jacob's prophecy (Gen 49:10). He reads the tabernacle at Shiloh as a sign that its worship would be fulfilled in a "greater and more perfect tabernacle." Benson quotes Matthew Henry saying the same. (https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/joshua-18.html; https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-1.htm)
- **Keil & Delitzsch (Lutheran scholars):** They argue the place wasn't picked mainly for being central. It was picked for its name, which recalled the promised Shiloh. They insist Joshua followed God's instruction, not his own judgment. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-18-commentary)
- **Calvin (Reformed):** As quoted in the Preacher's Homiletical Commentary, Calvin says the ark went to Shiloh because the area was fully conquered and safe from attack. (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/18-6.html)
- **From war to rest:** Jackman says the move from Gilgal shows a change from being on a war footing, with the main camp at Gilgal, to being at rest. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-18-commentary)
- **Unity:** Campbell (Bible Knowledge Commentary) notes that Joseph's tribes had just complained about their land (17:14–18). He thinks the tabernacle was set up at Shiloh partly to build national unity against that self-interest. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-18-commentary)
- **"Subdued":** Utley, a Baptist-trained teacher, says the verb "subdued" doesn't really describe the actual situation. (https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-18)
- **How long it stayed:** Estimates vary. JFB says over 300 years. Benson says about 350 but notes Ussher reckoned 328. Gill cites Jewish writers giving 369. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/jfb/joshua-18.html; https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-1.htm; https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-18.html)
- **Later decline:** Life Application Study Bible notes that Shiloh later became known for wickedness and idolatry (Ps 78; Jer 7). (https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-18-commentary)

**v. 2: Seven tribes still waiting**
- JFB says choosing Shiloh and moving the camp there interrupted the casting of lots, and various causes led to a long delay in resuming it. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/jfb/joshua-18.html)
- Matthew Henry says the seven tribes were sure of an inheritance but didn't know where, and seemed in no great hurry about it. (https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Jos/Jos_018.cfm)

**v. 3: "How long will you put off…?"**
- **Wesley (Methodist):** He offers two reasons for the delay. They may have thought fair division was impossible until the land was surveyed. They were also tired of war, had plenty, and didn't want new risks. (https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/joshua-18.html)
- **Gill (Baptist):** He adds that the plunder they enjoyed made them comfortable. Seeing other tribes unhappy with their lots may also have made them wait. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-18.html)
- **The Hebrew word:** Utley says the verb means to show oneself lazy; literally to relax or loosen. (https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-18)
- **Henry's application:** God has given us a title to the heavenly Canaan, but we are "slack" to possess it by faith, hope and joy. (https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Jos/Jos_018.cfm)
- **Henry on the danger:** While the tribes delayed, the Canaanites were regaining strength, which would make driving them out harder. (https://www.ccel.org/h/henry/mhc2/MHC06018.HTM)
- **Gaebelein:** Plenty made the people self-indulgent. He applies the verse to believers' neglect of salvation. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/gab/joshua-18.html)

**v. 4: Three men from each tribe**
- Barnes says there were 21 surveyors. They were to describe the land, especially its cities, so Joshua could make a first division according to each tribe's size. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-6.htm)
- JFB explains why a survey was needed. The lot decided where a tribe would live, not how much land it got. Joseph's complaint raised fears that other tribes would complain too. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-6.htm)
- A commentator quoted by Precept Austin praises Joshua's leadership here. A committee from all parties divided the land before the lot was used, which he calls a masterstroke! (https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-18-commentary)

**v. 5: Judah stays south, Joseph north**
- **Wesley:** Judah would not be disturbed, except where part of its land was given to another tribe. "North" means north of Judah, not of the whole land. (https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/joshua-18.html)
- **Precept Austin:** The message was "hands off" Judah's and Joseph's land. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-18-commentary)
- **Coffman:** He argues the seven new portions were meant to reduce Judah's and Ephraim's earlier allotments. Benjamin's borders therefore took priority, so there is no contradiction. (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/18-28.html)

**v. 6: Casting lots "before the LORD"**
- **Who cast the lots:** Utley notes that Joshua cast them, not the high priest, so perhaps they were not the Urim and Thummim. Either way, they expressed God's will. (https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-18)
- **The high priest:** Coffman says the high priest was surely there, and his presence is implied in "before the Lord." (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/18-6.html)
- **Why "before the Lord":** Wesley and Poole say it was so that God would be witness, judge and author of the division. Each tribe would then accept its lot, and its land would be held as sacred. (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/18-6.html; https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-6.htm)
- **Henry:** Each tribe should be thankful for its lot's advantages and accept its drawbacks. (https://www.ccel.org/h/henry/mhc2/MHC06018.HTM)
- **Pulpit Commentary:** The Hebrew is literally "write the land, seven parts," meaning a written report. It uses an unusual verb meaning "to throw." (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-6.htm)
- **Ellicott (Anglican):** He links this to Numbers 26. Larger tribes got more land, but the lot fixed where each tribe lived. (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/18-6.html)
- **Precept Austin:** It cites Proverbs 16:33 and counts "before the LORD" three times in vv. 6, 8 and 10. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-18-commentary)

**v. 7: Levites, and the tribes east of the Jordan**
- **What the Levites had instead:** Clarke lists sacrifices, offerings, tithes, firstfruits and redemption money for the firstborn. They had no land, and the Lord was their portion. Gill says the same, including the "perquisites" of the office. (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/18-7.html)
- **Henry:** Their inheritance was "a very honourable, comfortable, plentiful inheritance." (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/18-7.html)
- **Utley:** The Levites took the place of the firstborn in serving God. (https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-18)
- **Bible Hub study article:** It connects this to Hebrews 7, where the Levitical system typologically foreshadows the superior priesthood of Christ. (https://biblehub.com/q/Why_no_land_for_Levites_in_Joshua_18_7.htm)
- **Preacher's Homiletical Commentary:** The Shiloh lot didn't change God's earlier arrangements for Levi or for the two and a half eastern tribes. (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/18-6.html)

**v. 8: "Go and survey the land"**
- Utley says the commands repeat v. 4. Walking the land was itself a symbol of possession (Gen 13:17). (https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-18)
- Precept Austin links the walking to Joshua 1:3, "every place on which the sole of your foot treads." (https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-18-commentary)

**v. 9: The written survey**
- **How long it took:** Gill cites Josephus that the men came back after seven months. Measuring and mapping that much land would take a long time. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-18.html)
- **Literacy:** Utley says the verse shows the Israelites could read and write. (https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-18)
- **Josephus on "goodness":** Coffman quotes him saying Joshua divided the land by its quality, not just its size. (https://studylight.org/commentaries/bcc/joshua-18.html)
- **Henry:** God's providence protected the surveyors on their dangerous journey. (https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Jos/Jos_018.cfm)

**v. 10: The lots are cast**
- JFB: Doing this before the tabernacle linked the lot with God's approval. (https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/Jos/Jos_018.cfm)
- Precept Austin notes that some think Eleazar used the Urim and Thummim. The text simply says Joshua cast the lots. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-18-commentary)

**v. 11: Benjamin's lot, between Judah and Joseph**
- **How the lots worked:** Clarke and JFB suggest two urns, one holding the tribes' names and one the seven portions, drawn together. (https://www.studylight.org/bible/swe/sve/joshua/18-11.html; https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/Jos/Jos_018.cfm)
- **Ellicott (Anglican):** It was no accident. No wiser method could have been devised to secure an united Israel than to make Benjamin the link between rival tribes. He recalls how Judah and Joseph were reconciled over Benjamin in Genesis. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-11.htm)
- **Moses' blessing (Wesley, Poole, Benson):** This was the only spot where Deut 33:12 could be fulfilled. Benjamin sat next to Joseph, his full brother, and next to Judah, which it would later stand with in loyalty to David's throne and the temple. (https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/joshua-18.html; https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-11.htm)
- **Gill:** The lot was small ("little Benjamin," Ps 68:27) but pleasant and fruitful. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-11.htm)
- **Henry:** Little Benjamin needed great Joseph's protection, but had a better protector in the Lord (Deut 33:12). (https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Jos/Jos_018.cfm)
- **Coffman:** He calls the allotment providential. It put the future temple site in Benjamin and made Benjamin a buffer between Judah and Ephraim. His text cites "Deuteronomy 32:12," apparently meaning 33:12. (https://studylight.org/commentaries/bcc/joshua-18.html)
- **Bible Hub study notes:** They see Benjamin's place as a type of Christ, who unites God's divided people. (https://biblehub.com/joshua/18-11.htm)
- **Enduring Word:** Benjamin drew nearer in sympathy to Judah, and at the great division went with Judah altogether. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-18-19/)
- **Utley:** "Benjamin" means "son of the right hand." It was the tribe of Saul and of Paul. (https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-18)

**v. 12: Beth-aven**
- Utley says the name is a wordplay ("house of iniquity") that Hosea later used for Bethel. (https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-18)
- Ellicott says the northern border matched Ephraim's southern border. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-11.htm)

**v. 14: "This was the western side"**
- Henry points out that the KJV says this border "compassed the corner of the sea southward," even though no part of Benjamin came near the Mediterranean. (https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Jos/Jos_018.cfm)

**vv. 15–16: The southern border, Hinnom and the Jebusites**
- Precept Austin says this is the same line as Judah's northern border (15:5–9). (https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-18-commentary)
- **Rasmussen (atlas writer):** The detail around Jerusalem stands out. The text clearly places Jerusalem in Benjamin, even though a man of Judah (David) later took it. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/62610/)

**v. 17: Geliloth and the Stone of Bohan**
- **Utley:** "Geliloth" comes from a root meaning a circle of stones, possibly a sacred site. (https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-18)
- **Ellicott:** The Stone of Bohan must have been near the Jordan. He wonders whether Bohan set up his own memorial stone, as Joshua did for all Israel (4:8). (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-11.htm)

**v. 19: Beth-hoglah**
- Utley: the name means "place of the partridge." (https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-18)
- Coffman: Unger identifies it with ʿAin Hajlah, about 4 miles southeast of Jericho. (https://studylight.org/commentaries/bcc/joshua-18.html)

**vv. 21–27: Benjamin's cities**
- **Gangel:** Benjamin's land was small, but it held major cities: Jericho, Bethel, Gibeon, Mizpah, Ai and Jerusalem. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-18-commentary)
- **Avvim (v. 23):** Utley says this may refer to people from the southwest coast. (https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-18)
- **Chephar-ammoni (v. 24):** means "village of the Ammonites." (https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-18)
- **Geba (v. 24):** Barnes identifies it with modern Jeba, opposite Michmash. (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/18-28.html)
- **Irpeel (v. 27):** means "God heals"; location unknown. (https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-18)
- **Taralah (v. 27):** an unidentified site, probably northwest of Jerusalem. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/62610/)

**v. 28: Jebus (Jerusalem) and Gibeah**
- **Belonging to both tribes:** Gill says Jerusalem was partly Judah's and partly Benjamin's. Mount Zion was in Judah and Moriah, the temple mount, in Benjamin. Poole thinks it belonged first to Benjamin, with Judah sharing in it. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-28.htm)
- **Precept Austin:** It answers the 15:8 "problem" by saying the city lay inside Benjamin but on Judah's border, so both descriptions are right. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/62610/)
- **Ellicott:** No writer later than Joshua would likely have placed Jerusalem in Benjamin. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-11.htm)
- **Not yet captured:** Bible Hub notes that Benjamin held the city "on paper." It remained a Jebusite stronghold until David took it (2 Sam 5). (https://biblehub.com/joshua/18-28.htm)
- **Gibeah:** Pulpit and Cambridge identify Gibeath with "Gibeah of Saul" (Tuleil el-Fûl). It was the scene of Judges 19. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-28.htm)
- **Zelah:** the burial place of Saul and Jonathan (2 Sam 21:14). (https://biblehub.com/joshua/18-28.htm)
- **Kiriath:** Cambridge says this "Kirjath" was undiscovered and should not be confused with Kiriath-jearim, which belonged to Judah (v. 14). The BSB, however, reads "Kiriath-jearim" here. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-28.htm)
- **Josephus via Benson:** Benjamin's land was among the smallest but had the richest soil. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/18-28.htm)
